newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Esat Digifone expects 80 pct cover at launch.
newsitem.headline: Irish Esat Digifone expects 80 pct cover at launch.

text.p: Ireland's second mobile phone provider, Esat Digifone, said on Monday that it will have more than 80 percent population coverage when it goes live on March 21.
Esat, a consortium awarded Ireland's second mobile phone licence in 1995, is 40 percent owned by Norwegian state telecom company Telenor.
"We have had a massive response to our initial contacts with both personal and corporate customers," joint chief executive Barry Maloney told reporters at a pre-launch briefing.
Maloney said the experience of Telenor in operating a mobile network in Norway, which now has almost one million customers, has been integral in setting up the Esat service.
The Irish-based consortium said it had 200 dealer outlets across Ireland who will be able to start, on launch day, with complete support packages and promotional back-up.
The group has roaming agreements with 20 countries in place which it said represents 95 percent of the mobile phone traffic overseas.
In the UK it has agreements with Vodafone Group Plc and Cellnet and it said all EU countries are covered as well as Switzerland, Australia, South Africa, Hong Kong, New Zealand and Norway.
All Esat customers will have an 086 prefix, but will be able to retain their existing mobile number is they wish, Maloney said.
Esat will also offer guarantees to its customers that they will not be charged for dropped calls.

"We do not think it is fair that a customer should be charged for a call that has dropped," Maloney said. "Our promise to customers is that where we claim to have coverage, we do have coverage and this is reflected by our dropped call compensation.
Esat said if a dropped call is re-dialled within five minutes, up to one minutes worth of the dropped call will automatically credited onto the customers bill.
